concepts.title: Chemical Reactions and Their Signs
concepts.definition: A chemical reaction forms new substances: its signs include change of state, change of colour, evolution of gas and change of temperature - like magnesium burning to white magnesium oxide or quicklime slaking with heat in water.
concepts.key_idea: New substance formed is the surest sign - the others are its visible clues.

solution_steps.explain: Note the starting substances and their properties.
Colour, state, gas and temperature changes reveal reaction.

concepts.title: Writing and Balancing Chemical Equations
concepts.definition: A chemical equation writes a reaction with formulae and symbols of states; it is balanced by making atoms of each element equal on both sides, since mass can neither appear nor vanish - trial and adjustment of coefficients, never of formulae, achieves this.
concepts.key_idea: Change the coefficients, never the formulae: equal atoms on both sides is the law.

solution_steps.explain: List atoms of each element on both sides.
Change coefficients so both sides hold equal atoms.
Mark solid, liquid, gas or aqueous states in brackets.

concepts.title: Types of Chemical Reactions
concepts.definition: Reactions fall into families: combination joins reactants into one product, decomposition breaks one reactant into many, displacement swaps a more reactive element in, double displacement exchanges partners, and oxidation-reduction moves oxygen and hydrogen between substances.
concepts.key_idea: Five reaction families: combine, decompose, displace, double-displace and redox.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc101.txt sections on types of reactions
question_patterns: classify the given reactions into combination, decomposition and displacement

identify the substance oxidised and reduced in the given reaction
why is respiration an exothermic reaction - explain

solution_steps.explain: Joining indicates combination; splitting indicates decomposition.
A swap of partners shows displacement or double displacement.
Their gain or loss marks oxidation and reduction.

concepts.title: Effects of Oxidation in Daily Life
concepts.definition: Oxidation shows up in daily life as corrosion, like rusting of iron, and rancidity, when fats and oils in food oxidise; antioxidants, nitrogen flushing and refrigeration slow these unwanted oxidation reactions.
concepts.key_idea: Rust and rancidity are oxidation at work - prevention means blocking air and speed.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc101.txt sections on corrosion and rancidity
question_patterns: what is corrosion - give two examples from daily life

solution_steps.explain: Metal surfaces and food fats react with oxygen.
Corrosion weakens metals; rancidity spoils taste and smell.
Painting, galvanising, nitrogen flushing and cooling slow oxidation.
